name: Ted Decker

career.title: Corporate finance and lending roles (Pittsburgh and Sydney)
Business development, strategic planning and finance roles (incl. London and Atlanta)
Director of business valuation, rising to SVP of strategic business development and SVP of retail finance
Chief Merchant and Executive Vice President of Merchandising

background_rationale: Built his early career in banking and corporate finance at PNC, Scott Paper and Kimberly-Clark, and joined Home Depot in business valuation and finance before moving into merchandising and operations.

notable.summary: Home Depot agreed to acquire roofing and building-products distributor SRS Distribution for about $18.25 billion, its largest deal, to expand its business with professional contractors.
Home Depot agreed for its SRS subsidiary to acquire specialty building-products distributor GMS in a deal valued at about $5.5 billion, completed in September 2025.
Decker began a temporary medical leave on Aug. 12, 2026, expected to last a few months, with executives Ann-Marie Campbell and Richard McPhail overseeing operations and finance in the interim.

personal_story.hook: Ted Decker started mowing lawns at age 8 and ran a landscaping business before running Home Depot.
personal_story.summary: Decker grew up outside Erie, Pennsylvania, where he began mowing lawns at age 8 and built a landscaping business that he ran through high school. At William & Mary he majored in English while taking economics courses, and spent summers sealing driveways, buying supplies at local hardware stores. He pursued international banking after graduation, working for PNC in Sydney, then moved into corporate roles at Scott Paper and Kimberly-Clark, including in London. A recruiter's call reached him in his London office on the way to the airport and led to a lunch interview with Home Depot's CEO; he joined in 2000 as director of business valuation, hired by then-CFO Carol Tome, and was promoted repeatedly until becoming CEO in 2022.
